definition: TorchVision is PyTorch’s computer-vision package: datasets, image transforms and pretrained models like ResNet and ViT.
details: Part of the PyTorch project at Meta, maintained by the PyTorch Foundation.

explainer.lead: How to install TorchVision, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import torch
from torchvision.models import resnet50, ResNet50_Weights
from torchvision.io import decode_image

weights = ResNet50_Weights.DEFAULT
model = resnet50(weights=weights).eval()
img = weights.transforms()(decode_image("cat.jpg")).unsqueeze(0)
label = model(img).softmax(1).argmax().item()
print(weights.meta["categories"][label])

explainer.inAi: Start image classification or detection projects from pretrained backbones and fine-tune on your own pictures.
explainer.jsNote: TorchVision is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: TorchVision is the picture drawer of the PyTorch workshop: it hands you ready-made image collections, tools to tweak images, and models already trained to recognize things in pictures.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to pull datasets, apply image transforms and start from pretrained ResNet or ViT models rather than training from scratch. It is part of the PyTorch project at Meta and maintained by the PyTorch Foundation.
tiers.paperLevel: TorchVision is PyTorch's computer-vision package providing datasets, image transforms and pretrained models such as ResNet and ViT. It is part of the PyTorch project at Meta, maintained by the PyTorch Foundation.

explainer.example: A vision team loads a dataset, applies transforms and fine-tunes a pretrained ResNet, all from TorchVision.
